{"builder": {"source": "x", "name": "Aaron Levie", "handle": "levie", "bio": "ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI", "tweets": [{"id": "2119592025440092192", "text": "We’re moving from an era of AI where the output comes roughly at the rate that you can chat back and forth with the AI to work with you, to a period where you can set a problem for a set of agents to go off and do an arbitrarily large amount of work for you. This means productivity gains that are maybe 20-50% to gains that don’t really have an upper limit.

Agent swarms and the ability to fan out complex work across many agents doing tasks in parallel provide a massive unlock in a lot of spaces. This will lead to qualitatively different outcomes in my fields. 

This has already been seen across the coding domain. Next, cyber is almost entirely a problem space where more agents reviewing more things will lead to far better outcomes. We’re seeing the same now in many scientific fields, and this almost certainly will change life sciences. 

But this will increasingly be true in any field where you can parallelize computer-based work to complete something faster or do something at a totally different quality level. Which is actually are some of the most valuable domains of knowledge work today. 

Our brains aren’t really wired for the new scenario we’re heading into where compute becomes the variable that we can flex to solve any problem that we want. We’re used to thinking that the amount of time that goes into a task is correlated to the output that we get from it. And most domains of knowledge work or science have generally always been correlated with this. At no point in AI’s history is that more true than today.
